cases.valued_outcome: Synthetic bench exercise: keep a 6 W dummy electronics block at or below 48 C during minutes 5-15, while reducing fan sound relative to maximum-speed operation. Intermittent or zero fan operation may qualify. No real performance or human benefit is claimed.

hard_constraints.text: Use the 120 x 80 x 60 mm enclosure and specified bench parts; no purchases or powered refrigeration.
Outcome trials hold heater input at 6.0 W within 0.2 W; 3.0 W is a diagnostic control only.
Ambient starts between 25 and 28 C. Abort heating above 55 C block temperature; cool unpowered between trials.
A probe has at most four 15-minute heating trials within two hours including cooling and setup.
Changes remain removable and leave cable access open. The thermal target applies only to this mockup.

observations.text: Synthetic geometry: a 40 mm fan draws through an inlet; the side outlet center is 30 mm from the inlet center.
At 6.0 W, fixed 100 percent fan duty and 26.0 C ambient, block temperatures at minutes 5, 10 and 15 are 43.8, 46.3 and 47.2 C.
Same-run inlet temperatures are 28.1, 31.0 and 32.0 C; outlet temperatures are 33.0, 35.8 and 36.7 C.
A separate 3.0 W maximum-speed run ends at 36.5 C block and 27.4 C inlet after 15 minutes, with 26.0 C ambient.
Baseline sound is 46 dBA at 0.5 m; unpowered bench background is 32 dBA at that position.
Boundary anomaly: a stationary cardboard sheet 20 mm beside the outlet changes minute-15 inlet temperature to 34.0 C. Its block temperature is unrecorded.
Existing thermostat rule commands 100 percent duty above 44 C, zero below 42 C and retains the prior command between thresholds. No controlled trace is supplied.

resources.text: Stipulated bench equipment: secured resistive dummy heater, enclosure, fused adjustable DC supply and inline power meter; 3.0 W and 6.0 W are available settings.
40 mm fan and manual PWM controller with 0, 50 and 100 percent settings; an operator can implement O7 every 30 seconds.
Four thermocouples labeled block, inlet, outlet and ambient, with stated 0.5 C accuracy and four-channel display; readings can be recorded manually every 30 seconds.
Sound meter with 1 dBA resolution, fixed stand at 0.5 m and timer; three 10-second readings are feasible at minutes 5, 10 and 15. Calibration is unspecified.
Two 100 x 100 mm cardstock sheets, removable tape, scissors and ruler permit external outlet-air separation or redirection without touching heater or blades.
Removable 40 x 40 x 10 mm aluminum sink, reusable thermal pad, notebook and two-hour bench slot.
Smoke tracer, airflow meter, acoustic spectrum analyzer and environmental chamber are absent; direct flow-field measurements are unavailable.

cases.preferred_dependency: The operator treats continuous maximum-speed fan operation as necessary for the thermal target. Only one full-load configuration has a complete trace, leaving necessity questionable.
cases.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Unobserved hypothesis: outlet air returns to the nearby inlet, raises inlet temperature, reduces cooling and prolongs thermostat-commanded fan operation, sustaining outlet discharge. Test outlet separation present/absent at fixed maximum duty first, then under O7, holding power and probe positions fixed. Existing temperatures do not establish recirculation or feedback.

parent_operations.text: Remove heat through fan-driven inlet-to-outlet airflow; duty and external outlet geometry can be examined independently.
Transfer block heat through the removable thermal pad and sink. The exposed block face interfaces conductive cooling with airflow cooling.

available_observables.text: Block temperatures every 30 seconds, maximum during minutes 5-15 and any 55 C abort.
Simultaneous inlet, outlet and ambient readings; calculate inlet-minus-ambient and outlet-minus-inlet with sensor limits.
Fan commands every 30 seconds, commanded on-time and threshold transitions; command does not measure airflow.
Sound at fixed times and distance, with unpowered background before each trial.
Power readings and sketched sheet/sink placement. Reverse order across paired trials; start with block within 1 C of ambient.

unknowns.text: Airflow, recirculated fraction and actual speed response to PWM are unmeasured.
Placement bias and ambient drift may explain inlet warming; outlet separation may alter resistance.
Cooling beyond 15 minutes and behavior in real electronics remain conditional.

ordinary_archive.relation: Forced convection ordinarily exports heat; duty need not scale directly with cooling.
ordinary_archive.probe: Repeat O2 twice from the prescribed cool start; collect M1-M4.
ordinary_archive.limits: Repeatability does not establish fan necessity or recirculation.

ordinary_archive.operation: Apply the existing 44/42 C thermostat rule.
ordinary_archive.relation: Feedback can reduce fan time when passive cooling reaches the lower threshold.
ordinary_archive.probe: Run one 6 W trial with 30-second manual decisions and command logging.
ordinary_archive.limits: Manual sampling can overshoot; lower on-time alone does not establish thermal compliance.

ordinary_archive.operation: Attach the sink while retaining maximum fan duty.
ordinary_archive.relation: Added conductive area can reduce block-to-air thermal resistance.
ordinary_archive.probe: Compare a sink-present trial with matched baseline and pad placement.
ordinary_archive.limits: Contact variation and thermal mass confound mechanism; benefit may be transient.

cases.valued_outcome: Synthetic CI diagnosis exercise: correctly identify and cite the seeded initiating failure within 12 simulated minutes using at most one full-suite rerun. Retained evidence may suffice. No real productivity or human benefit is claimed.

hard_constraints.text: Use only this deterministic model; no real CI, project execution or incident operators.
Diagnosis must cite component, message and run number from evidence actually viewed; unsupported fixture-answer guessing is invalid.
Budget is 12 simulated minutes. Full rerun costs four minutes, focused rerun two, and each view action one.
Report diagnosis and cost; losing the initiating record fails the outcome even if work is faster.
Score only after committing a diagnosis. Fixture truth is procedurally concealed from the exercising role; no production data are supplied.

observations.text: Synthetic full run has components B1-B10 and 90 numbered lines. Line 8 says B2 CONFIG missing region; lines 68 and 74 contain downstream B7 and B9 errors.
Every other line says progress only, with component labels cycling B1-B10 by line-number modulo ten.
Default view opens the newest run at lines 51-90. Full view exposes lines 1-90 for the selected run.
New full runs reset default selection. History retains two named runs; run-1 and run-2 persist until another full run advances history.
Stipulated trace: time 0, run-1 tail viewed; time 1, full rerun requested; time 5, run-2 tail opened; time 6, B7 selected for follow-up. No initiating diagnosis was submitted.
Boundary anomaly: focused B7 output has ten lines; line 2 says B7 prerequisite B2 unavailable, with progress elsewhere. It omits the B2 configuration message.
Focused B2 output has ten lines; line 2 says B2 CONFIG missing region, with progress elsewhere. Focused views expose all ten lines; the failure stays constant.

resources.text: O1-O3 and O6-O7 completely specify the synthetic log recipe. Paper or spreadsheet rows can instantiate it; no external fixture file is promised.
Notebook, paper table or spreadsheet can represent two-slot history and selected view, advancing full runs exactly as O4 specifies.
A simulated clock uses C3 costs; completion is instantaneous in wall time after charging minutes. One tabletop operator can execute actions and log them.
O1 supplies the scoring key. A covered answer sheet or scoring role checks committed citations; within-packet blinding is procedural, not guaranteed.
Controls reset to completed run-1 at time zero; tail/full selection is independent of no rerun, full rerun or the specified focused rerun.
A negative fixture replaces line 8 with progress while retaining other rules. It has no seeded root and cannot count as successful root diagnosis.
Live CI, source changes, automated blame tools and real analyst timing data are absent.

cases.preferred_dependency: The preferred procedure requires a fresh full-suite rerun before diagnosis because fresh execution supposedly provides indispensable context. The unchanged fixture and retained history make this necessity questionable.
cases.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Unobserved hypothesis: full rerunning resets selection to a tail without the initiating error; downstream-only evidence prompts another full rerun, resetting selection again. Cross rerun/no-rerun with tail/full view under identical budgets and log visibility and following actions. O5 describes a synthetic sequence, not its decision causes.

parent_operations.text: Execute full or focused jobs to generate named runs, charging time and changing history/default selection.
Select and inspect retained evidence through tail/full view. Run identity and line selection interface generation with diagnosis.

available_observables.text: Action sequence, simulated start/end times, requested component and full-rerun count.
Selected run and visible line interval after every action; mark initiating-record visibility.
Committed component/message/run citation, scored against the fixture and viewed records.
History before/after reruns, including lost old runs on a third full run.
Next action after downstream-only versus root-containing views. Compare scripted policies or separate tabletop repetitions without population-behavior claims.

unknowns.text: Real analysts may rerun for reasons unrelated to visibility.
Actual CI cost and cognitive effort are absent; action costs are stipulated.
Nondeterministic, changing or multiple-root failures may favor fresh execution.

ordinary_archive.operation: Rerun the full suite once and inspect its default tail.
ordinary_archive.relation: Fresh execution reproduces the fixed failure, but only the last forty lines are visible.
ordinary_archive.probe: Charge four minutes plus one view; record errors and any supported diagnosis.
ordinary_archive.limits: Line 8 is absent by construction; real analyst behavior is untested.

ordinary_archive.operation: Open the full retained log and locate its first error.
ordinary_archive.relation: Earlier preserved output can expose the initiating record omitted by the tail.
ordinary_archive.probe: View run-1 fully for one minute and cite its earliest error.
ordinary_archive.limits: First error is root only by fixture definition; concurrency may invalidate this heuristic.

ordinary_archive.relation: Focused execution can reveal an immediate prerequisite at lower modeled cost.
ordinary_archive.probe: Charge two minutes plus one view and inspect O6 output.
ordinary_archive.limits: B2 is named, but the initiating configuration message required by C2 remains absent.

cases.valued_outcome: Synthetic water-and-dye exercise: produce three elevation samples with normalized blue-channel attenuation spread at most 4 percent of their mean by 120 seconds, reducing stirring time if feasible. This is a bounded uniformity proxy; no real chemical or human benefit is claimed.

hard_constraints.text: Use 150 mL tap water and 0.30 mL blue food dye in the 250 mL beaker; no other chemicals or heating.
Use one dye bottle and locked camera settings per comparison block; begin each trial with a fresh recipe and rinsed vessel.
Mixing ends by second 105, allowing fifteen quiet seconds before sampling starts at second 120.
At most six trials fit a 90-minute session. Use the spill tray and stop if liquid escapes.
Report sample readings, stirring duration and target failures; stable side images alone cannot establish success.

observations.text: Synthetic liquid depth is 55 mm. Side-image regions are 5 mm high, centered 10, 28 and 45 mm above the bottom.
Preferred rule checks side-image spread every five seconds and continues 900 rpm until three successive checks are at most 4 percent, subject to C3.
Stipulated 900 rpm spread at seconds 30, 35 and 40 is 11, 3 and 12 percent; central surface depression is about 12 mm deep.
A separate 300 rpm trial gives spreads 8, 6 and 5 percent at those times and approximately 3 mm surface depression.
In the 300 rpm trial, stirring stopped at second 60; final vial attenuations were 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread.
Boundary anomaly: 900 rpm images contain transient bright specks crossing the middle region; isolated bubble measurements and matched final vial readings are absent.
Three reference vials from one manually premixed aliquot give 0.205, 0.207 and 0.206. This synthetic repeatability is not calibration.

resources.text: Stipulated beaker, spill tray, 150 mL measuring cylinder, water, food dye and 1 mL syringe graduated every 0.01 mL.
Magnetic stirrer, 20 mm bar and nominal manual 0, 300, 600 and 900 rpm settings; no independent tachometer.
Fixed USB camera and diffuse LED backlight with locked exposure/white balance. Manual blue-region means can be entered in a spreadsheet every five seconds.
Three identical clear 5 mL vials and sampling syringe marked for 10, 28 and 45 mm. Withdraw 1 mL per depth within ten seconds after second 120; alternate order between paired trials.
Water-only and common-aliquot references per block. Attenuation equals 1 minus sample blue intensity divided by water-reference intensity; spread equals max-minus-min divided by mean.
A needle-free 20 mL syringe permits low-position withdrawal and upper-side return; marked positions, timer and notebook make transfer counts repeatable.
Microscope, dissolved-gas probe, calibrated spectrophotometer and concentration standards are absent; bubble fraction and absolute concentration are unmeasurable.

cases.preferred_dependency: The preferred procedure treats sustained 900 rpm stirring until stable optical readings as necessary for uniformity. Lower-speed sample readings and differing optical/sample measures question that necessity.
cases.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Unobserved hypothesis: high-speed stirring entrains bubbles and perturbs side-image attenuation; the stop rule interprets fluctuations as incomplete mixing, prolonging agitation and disturbances. Compare fixed-duration 300/900 rpm runs and brief stir-off observation intervals at matched times, retaining independent final-vial checks. Specks do not establish bubbles or concentration uniformity.

parent_operations.text: Rotate liquid with the stirrer, choosing speed and duration independently; camera spread is the current feedback interface.
Redistribute bulk liquid low-to-high using the 20 mL syringe; the shared volume permits comparison or combination with rotation.

available_observables.text: Three side-region attenuations, frames and normalized spread every five seconds.
Final depth-vial attenuation, sampling order and normalized spread after the common quiet interval.
Commanded speed, start/stop times, total stirring seconds and each syringe transfer.
Ruler-estimated surface depression and speck-containing frame count; these do not identify bubbles.
Reference repeatability, recipe and camera checks. Reverse speed order across pairs and hold dye-addition location fixed.

unknowns.text: Specks may be bubbles, reflections or undissolved dye; causal contribution is unverified.
Sampling and transfers can disturb gradients; optical concentration calibration is absent.
Other viscosities, solutes, vessel sizes and continuous processes remain untested.

ordinary_archive.operation: Use the existing 900 rpm optical stop rule.
ordinary_archive.relation: Agitation ordinarily accelerates mixing; the image signal serves as completion proxy.
ordinary_archive.probe: Record checks until passing or second 105, then collect final vials.
ordinary_archive.limits: Fluctuations may have other causes; the cap can end unresolved runs.

ordinary_archive.operation: Stir at 300 rpm for sixty seconds.
ordinary_archive.relation: Lower-speed circulation can mix a small volume with less surface disturbance.
ordinary_archive.probe: Repeat O5 with fresh recipe and final-vial checks.
ordinary_archive.limits: One synthetic trace does not establish repeatability or optimal speed.

ordinary_archive.operation: Make five 20 mL low-to-high transfers over thirty seconds.
ordinary_archive.relation: Bulk redistribution ordinarily offers an alternative to continuous rotation.
ordinary_archive.probe: Use marked positions, log transfers and collect final vials.
ordinary_archive.limits: Transfers may entrain air and vary with hand speed; scale-up is unknown.

cases.valued_outcome: Synthetic spreadsheet exercise: correctly apply exactly three status corrections to immutable keys within ten simulated minutes without any incorrect-key write. Fewer refreshes may qualify. No actual financial records, operational savings or human benefit are claimed.

hard_constraints.text: Use only the eight invented records and scheduled snapshots; no live system, account or external message.
Target statuses are K2, K5 and K7 checked; the other five remain unchecked.
Source scores are read-only. Modify only checked status and log every actual written key.
Ten-minute budget: refresh, inspect/select and commit each cost one simulated minute; actions are sequential.
Load the latest source snapshot before final submission. Intermediate freshness frequency is flexible; correct keys and statuses are mandatory.

observations.text: S0 has K1-K8 scores 80, 70, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10; all statuses unchecked. Sort descending score, then ascending key for ties.
S1 is available at minute 2: K2 changes to 25, K5 to 75. S2 is available at minute 5: K7 changes to 75, K1 to 35. Other scores persist; source statuses do not change.
Refresh loads the snapshot available at completion and resorts. Row 2 contains K2 under S0, K5 under S1 and K7 under S2.
Editor retains selected row number and typed checked value across refresh. Commit writes the key currently occupying that row without key confirmation.
Stipulated trace: select K2 at row 2 during minutes 0-1; refresh during 1-2 loads S1; commit during 2-3 writes checked to K5. This is an invented wrong-target write.
Boundary anomaly: S2 gives K5 and K7 equal score 75; tie ordering places K5 first. Score alone cannot identify the intended key.
Preferred procedure refreshes immediately before every commit and requests another refresh on intended/actual key mismatch. No completed correction trace is supplied.

resources.text: O1-O2 fully specify all source snapshots, instantiable on paper or spreadsheet; no external workbook or endpoint is promised.
A table shows key, score and status. Row-selection persistence follows O4 manually; local statuses persist by key through refresh.
Notebook and simulated clock follow C4; S0 starts loaded at time zero. Snapshot eligibility advances with elapsed time even without refresh.
Correction checklist names K2, K5, K7. Keys can be inspected before commit; scoring compares final statuses and logged writes with C2.
Diagnostic controls hold source on S0 or enable O2, and retain row binding or enact immutable-key binding. Sorting and tie rule stay fixed unless explicitly varied.
Replay identical initial data and actions. No-refresh diagnosis cannot satisfy final freshness after minute 2; a final S2 refresh is feasible within ten minutes.
Production connectors, spreadsheet macros, collaboration telemetry and human usability participants are absent.

cases.preferred_dependency: The preferred workflow treats refresh before every commit as necessary for reliable correction. Targets do not depend on changing scores, and C5 permits other refresh schedules, questioning necessity.
cases.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Unobserved process hypothesis: refresh reorders selection, row-bound commit miswrites, and mismatch requests another refresh that may reorder the next selected row and repeat the error. O5 stipulates one miswrite, not repeated feedback. Cross changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding under identical actions; record intended, selected and actual keys.

parent_operations.text: Refresh read-only source scores and reorder rows according to the snapshot schedule.
Select targets and commit statuses. Selection identity interfaces refresh with editing; row-bound and key-bound replay are available.

available_observables.text: Action times, refresh count and loaded snapshot after every action.
Displayed key order, retained row number and intended key before/after refresh.
Actual key/value of every commit; count incorrect-key writes even if repaired.
Final status map, exact-target correctness and latest-snapshot compliance.
Mismatch-triggered refresh requests in scripted replay. Compare four controls with identical initial state/action schedule; claims concern the model only.

unknowns.text: Real editor selection may bind to row or immutable identity; O4 is synthetic.
Real detection rates and interruption costs are absent; modeled action costs are deterministic.
Concurrent status changes, deleted keys and snapshot-load failures are outside the model.

ordinary_archive.operation: Refresh, reselect intended key, then commit each correction.
ordinary_archive.relation: Reselection after sorting can repair stale selection while maintaining frequent freshness.
ordinary_archive.probe: Charge three actions per target and finish with the latest snapshot.
ordinary_archive.limits: Consumes most of the budget and depends on key reading; score ties are insufficient.

ordinary_archive.operation: Batch corrections from S0, then refresh once.
ordinary_archive.relation: Deferring reordering can stabilize positions while preserving final freshness.
ordinary_archive.probe: Perform three select/commit pairs, then refresh; check actual keys and S2.
ordinary_archive.limits: Targets are source-independent here; changing targets or deletions may defeat batching.

ordinary_archive.operation: Inspect immutable key immediately before row-bound commit.
ordinary_archive.relation: Identity checking can detect a different record occupying the selected row.
ordinary_archive.probe: Replay O5 with an extra inspection; log detection, reselection and cost.
ordinary_archive.limits: Detection is scripted, not measured human capability; inspection consumes budget.

independence_note: No prior candidates, strategy prompts or results were read
